newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Board positions seen for ANZ's Don Mercer.
newsitem.headline: Board positions seen for ANZ's Don Mercer.

text.p: Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd (ANZ) chief Don Mercer will likely be offered numerous board positions when he retires later this year, recruitment experts said on Thursday.

"His future lies being a chairman or non-executive director of two, three four, five organisations or companies, whatever," said Guy Pease, principal of Pro-Ned, a search firm devoted solely to the appointment of non-executive directors.
"That's his next move I would say, without a doubt."
Mercer's surprise announcement on Wednesday came after almost five years as ANZ chief and after the release of a record half year profit which outstripped its three main rivals.
Pease said Mercer will be keenly sought because of his ability to be outspoken but genial at the same time.

"Someone with that sort of banking background, experience on the international scene, managing a big organisation and dealing with a board from a chief executive's role - I think he could go fairly far and wide," Pease said.
ANZ spokeswoman Tania Hudson said Mercer has given no indication about what his future plans might be.
"All he has said is he going to have a think about what he is going to do," Hudson said.
She said Mercer has about six months to decide his future and although no specific time has been set for Mercer's retirement, sometime in November was likely.

The Scottish-born banker took over ANZ in October 1992, when the bank was suffering from the recession of the early 1990s and writing off loans to failed property developers from the credit binge of the late 1980s.
Mercer was only six weeks into the job when ANZ posted a A$579 million loss for the year to September 30, 1992.
On Wednesday, ANZ recorded an 18 percent rise in net profit to A$615 million in the six months ended March 31, 1997.
A partner of a Sydney-based executive recruitment firm said Mercer may decide to move back to the United Kingdom where he worked for many years for Anglo-Dutch oil company Royal Dutch/Shell Group.
"He is a keen golfer so he may want to go back to the home of the game," he said.
Mercer's successor at ANZ has been the subject of much speculation.

Analysts said likely candidates include former Bank of Melbourne Ltd managing director David Airey, who joined ANZ earlier this year to manage its New Zealand operations and the head of ANZ's retail banking, Peter Hawkins.
